title: Physics of the flying fish: glide data and Thompson's flight envelope
headline: No accessible source gives body mass, fin area and a measured airspeed for the same flying fish: the #50 glide table has 27 rows from 7 fetched sources, 6 species or groups, only 2 with first-hand measurements, and every glide speed is a second-hand quote of 1941-1994 work behind paywalls. On what exists, the flying fish is inside Thompson's envelope: from its own measured wing loading and lift coefficient (Park and Choi 2010) its minimum lift-supported speed is 9.85 m/s, and quoted field glide speeds are 10 to 20 m/s. The scaling law itself (speed grows as the square root of wing loading) is inconclusive: 2 glider taxa and 6 powered-flier taxa with both numbers, the latter spanning 0.93 decades of wing loading against the pre-registered minimum of 1. Whether fin muscles could power level flight cannot be told: no source gives the muscle numbers. Birds excluded (Aves holdout). Pre-registered before any value was read; 97 logged searches and fetches; 4 unsigned nanopub drafts; formal statements with the Lean thread. New: the bridge figure places the five wind-tunnel specimens (pectoral length over body length at most 0.63 to 0.66, an upper bound) inside the measured flying-fish range of Daane et al. 2021 (median 0.687, 49 MCZ specimens, recounted and agreeing with the Genotype thread), far above halfbeaks and needlefish; a deck figure of the v_min band against every published speed; sources on hover on both.
